takeaway: The defecation reflex starts at an intrarectal pressure of 18 mmHg, afferents reach S1-3, and efferents activate parasympathetic myenteric neurons.

question.text: Concerning the defecation reflex, which statement is correct?
question.say: Concerning the defecation reflex, which statement is correct?

answer.text: Efferent impulses activate post-ganglionic parasympathetic neurons of the myenteric plexus.
answer.say: Efferent impulses activate post-ganglionic parasympathetic neurons of the myenteric plexus.

lines.text: The reflex is triggered when rectal pressure reaches 18 millimetres of mercury, not 80.
Afferent impulses travel to sacral segments one to three.
The efferent limb activates parasympathetic neurons in the myenteric plexus.
Parasympathetic stimulation relaxes the internal anal sphincter, not sympathetic.
To resist, the pudendal nerve increases the tone of the external sphincter.
So the correct statement is the efferent, myenteric plexus option.
